newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn in mostly good-excellent condition.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn in mostly good-excellent condition.

text.p: The Nebraska corn crop was in mostly good to excellent condition as of Sunday, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Fourteen percent of the crop was excellent, 59 percent good, 25 percent fair and two percent poor.
However, many reports indicated that corn leaves were rolling due to a lack of moisture and topsoil moisture supplies were becoming short.
Topsoil moisture was rated eight percent very short, 34 percent short, 56 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
Winter wheat conditions were rated one percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 47 percent good and two percent excellent.
Soybeans were 97 percent emerged, ahead of 87 percent a year ago and 88 percent average. The crop was rated three percent poor, 29 percent fair, 59 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Pasture and range conditions rated one percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 28 percent fair, 59 percent good and two percent excellent.
